fr.B: Jérémie dit à Seraya : « Quand tu arriveras à Babylone, veille à lire toutes ces paroles à haute voix,
fr.R: Jérémie a dit à Seraya : « Quand tu arriveras à Babylone, n’oublie pas de lire toutes ces paroles à voix haute.

sw.L: Naye Yeremia akamwambia Seraya, "Utakapofika Babeli, angalia uyasome maneno haya yote kwa sauti,
sw.B: Yeremia akamwambia Seraya, "Utakapofika Babeli, hakikisha unayasoma maneno haya yote kwa sauti,
sw.R: Yeremia akamwambia Seraya, "Ukifika Babeli, hakikisha unayasoma maneno haya yote kwa sauti.

vi.L: Giê-rê-mi nói với Sê-ra-gia: "Khi ông đến Ba-by-lôn, hãy lo đọc to tất cả những lời này,
vi.B: Giê-rê-mi nói với Sê-ra-gia: "Khi đến Ba-by-lôn, ông hãy nhớ đọc to tất cả những lời này,
vi.R: Giê-rê-mi bảo Sê-ra-gia: "Khi đến Ba-by-lôn, ông nhớ đọc to tất cả những lời này.

ko.L: 그리고 예레미야가 스라야에게 말했다. "당신이 바빌론에 이르거든, 이 모든 말씀을 반드시 소리 내어 읽으시오.
ko.B: 예레미야가 스라야에게 말했다. "당신이 바빌론에 도착하면, 이 모든 말씀을 꼭 소리 내어 읽으시오.
ko.R: 예레미야가 스라야에게 말했다. "바빌론에 도착하면 이 모든 말씀을 꼭 큰 소리로 읽으시오.

pt.L: E Jeremias disse a Seraías: "Quando você chegar à Babilônia, veja [que] leia em voz alta todas estas palavras,
pt.B: Jeremias disse a Seraías: "Quando você chegar à Babilônia, trate de ler em voz alta todas estas palavras,
pt.R: Jeremias disse a Seraías: "Quando você chegar à Babilônia, não deixe de ler todas estas palavras em voz alta.

decisions.choice: and you will see, and you will read: see to it that you read
decisions.reason: The two verbs together mean "take care to read" (compare Exodus 25:40). It may also mean "look around you and read": read where the city can be seen.

decisions.choice: read aloud: proclaim the words in Babylon itself
decisions.reason: The verb means to read aloud. Whether many heard it or Seraiah read it for God alone, the word against Babylon was spoken in Babylon, as a prophetic act (verse 63).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes in verse 64
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's instructions run to the end of verse 64; the words Seraiah is to say take single quotation marks. Readable ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: ông (Jeremiah to Seraiah)
decisions.reason: Seraiah is a royal officer, Baruch's brother; the prophet speaks to him with the respectful "ông", as to the officials in chapters 36-38.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaks to Seraiah, a royal officer, in 하오체; Seraiah's words to God (verse 62) are 합쇼체
decisions.reason: As with the officials in chapters 36-40; the prayer form is the terms note's 합쇼체 with "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여".

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ יְהוָה֙ אַתָּ֨ה דִבַּ֜רְתָּ אֶל־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ לְהַכְרִית֔וֹ לְבִלְתִּ֤י הֱיֽוֹת־בּוֹ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֔ב לְמֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה כִּֽי־שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will say: Yahweh, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that not [is] in it an inhabitant, from man to beast, for desolations of forever it will be.

en.L: and say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that there will be no one dwelling in it, from human to animal, for it will be a desolation forever.'
en.B: and say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy this place, so that nothing will live in it, neither people nor animals, and it will be a desolation forever.'
en.R: Then say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy this place. No people or animals will live here. It will be an empty ruin forever.'

es.L: y di: “{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has hablado acerca de este lugar, que lo destruirías, de modo que no haya en él quien habite, desde el hombre hasta el animal, porque será desolación perpetua”.
es.B: y di: “{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has dicho que destruirás este lugar, de modo que nada viva en él, ni personas ni animales, y que será una desolación para siempre”.
es.R: Luego di: “{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has dicho que destruirás este lugar. Ni personas ni animales vivirán aquí. Será una ruina vacía para siempre”.

fr.L: et dis : “{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as parlé au sujet de ce lieu, pour le retrancher, afin qu’il n’y ait plus personne qui y habite, depuis l’humain jusqu’à la bête, car il sera une désolation pour toujours.”
fr.B: et dis : “{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détruirais ce lieu, si bien que rien n’y vivra, ni humains ni bêtes, et qu’il sera une désolation pour toujours.”
fr.R: Puis dis : “{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détruirais ce lieu. Ni les gens ni les animaux n’y vivront. Ce sera une ruine vide pour toujours.”

sw.L: na kusema, 'Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umesema juu ya mahali hapa, kwamba utapakatilia mbali, hata pasiwe na mkaaji ndani yake, tangu mwanadamu hadi mnyama, kwa maana patakuwa ukiwa milele.'
sw.B: na kusema, 'Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umesema kwamba utapaangamiza mahali hapa, hata kisiwepo kitu chochote kinachoishi ndani yake, wala watu wala wanyama, napo patakuwa ukiwa milele.'
sw.R: Kisha useme, 'Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umesema kwamba utapaangamiza mahali hapa. Hakuna watu wala wanyama watakaoishi hapa. Patakuwa magofu matupu milele.'

vi.L: và nói: 'Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán về nơi này rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ hủy diệt nó, để không còn ai ở trong đó, từ loài người đến thú vật, vì nó sẽ hoang vu đời đời.'
vi.B: và nói: 'Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ hủy diệt nơi này, để không còn gì sống trong đó, cả người lẫn thú vật, và nó sẽ hoang vu đời đời.'
vi.R: Rồi hãy nói: 'Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ hủy diệt nơi này. Sẽ không có người hay thú vật nào sống ở đây. Nó sẽ là một đống đổ nát vắng tanh mãi mãi.'

ko.L: 그리고 말하시오. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 이곳에 관하여 이곳을 끊어 버리시겠다고, 그래서 사람부터 짐승까지 그 안에 사는 것이 하나도 없게 하시겠다고 말씀하셨습니다. 이곳이 영원한 황무지가 될 것입니다.'
ko.B: 그리고 이렇게 말하시오. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 이곳을 멸망시키시겠다고 말씀하셨습니다. 그래서 사람도 짐승도 여기에 살지 못하고, 이곳이 영원히 황무지가 될 것이라고 하셨습니다.'
ko.R: 그러고 나서 이렇게 말하시오. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 이곳을 멸망시키시겠다고 말씀하셨습니다. 사람도 짐승도 여기에서 살지 못할 것입니다. 이곳은 영원히 텅 빈 폐허가 될 것입니다.'

pt.L: e diga: '{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} falaste a respeito deste lugar, que o eliminarias, para que não haja nele morador, desde o ser humano até o animal, pois será uma desolação para sempre.'
pt.B: e diga: '{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} disseste que destruirias este lugar, para que nada viva nele, nem pessoas nem animais, e que ele seria uma desolação para sempre.'
pt.R: Depois diga: '{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} disseste que vais destruir este lugar. Nem pessoas nem animais vão viver aqui. Vai ser uma ruína vazia para sempre.'

decisions.choice: to cut it off ... from human to animal ... a desolation forever: the words of the oracle
decisions.reason: Seraiah repeats the oracle's own sentence: no one living there, human or animal (50:3; 51:29, 43), and a desolation forever (51:26). He holds God to his word in the place it concerns.

decisions.choice: LORD, you have spoken: Seraiah speaks to God
decisions.reason: The words are a prayer addressed to the LORD, not a message to the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: What Seraiah is to say is quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, so it takes single quotation marks. The LORD is addressed without "O", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} (vocative, no article)
decisions.reason: YHWH addressed directly, as set in the terms note.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA" for the vocative
decisions.reason: The vocative form set in the Swahili Psalms (19:15); the free "wewe" for God takes the deity span.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}" in the vocative, without article
decisions.reason: The vocative as the French terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: Lạy CHÚA; Ngài
decisions.reason: Seraiah speaks to God as the terms note sets for prayer: "lạy CHÚA", with no "O", and "Ngài" for "you".

decisions.choice: SENHOR (vocative, no article); tu (Seraiah to God); você (Jeremiah to Seraiah)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks to Seraiah with "você", as people speak to each other; the words Seraiah is to say to God take "tu" with deity_pronoun spans, and the vocative "SENHOR" takes no article, as 5:3 sets it.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ כְּכַלֹּ֣תְךָ֔ לִקְרֹ֖א אֶת־הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה תִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ אֶ֔בֶן וְהִשְׁלַכְתּ֖וֹ אֶל־תּ֥וֹךְ פְּרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be when you finish to read this scroll, you will tie on it a stone and you will throw it into [the] midst of [the] Euphrates,

en.L: And when you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
en.B: When you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
en.R: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it. Throw it into the middle of the Euphrates River.

es.L: Y cuando termines de leer este rollo, átale una piedra y échalo en medio del Éufrates,
es.B: Cuando hayas terminado de leer este rollo, átale una piedra y arrójalo en medio del Éufrates,
es.R: Cuando termines de leer este rollo, átale una piedra. Tíralo en medio del río Éufrates.

fr.L: Et quand tu auras achevé de lire ce rouleau, attache-y une pierre et jette-le au milieu de l’Euphrate,
fr.B: Quand tu auras fini de lire ce rouleau, attache-y une pierre et jette-le au milieu de l’Euphrate,
fr.R: Quand tu auras fini de lire ce rouleau, attache-y une pierre. Jette-le au milieu de l’Euphrate.

sw.L: Na utakapomaliza kulisoma gombo hili, ufunge jiwe juu yake, ulitupe katikati ya Frati,
sw.B: Utakapomaliza kulisoma gombo hili, lifunge jiwe, ulitupe katikati ya Frati,
sw.R: Ukimaliza kulisoma gombo hili, lifunge jiwe. Litupe katikati ya Mto Frati.

vi.L: Khi ông đã đọc xong cuộn sách này, hãy buộc một hòn đá vào nó và ném nó xuống giữa sông Ơ-phơ-rát,
vi.B: Khi ông đã đọc xong cuộn sách này, hãy buộc một hòn đá vào nó và ném nó xuống giữa sông Ơ-phơ-rát,
vi.R: Khi đọc xong cuộn sách này, ông hãy buộc một hòn đá vào nó. Hãy ném nó xuống giữa sông Ơ-phơ-rát.

ko.L: 그리고 당신이 이 두루마리를 다 읽거든, 거기에 돌을 매어 유프라테스 강 한가운데에 던지시오.
ko.B: 이 두루마리를 다 읽은 다음에는, 거기에 돌을 매달아 유프라테스 강 한가운데에 던지시오.
ko.R: 이 두루마리를 다 읽은 다음에는 거기에 돌을 매다시오. 그리고 그것을 유프라테스 강 한가운데에 던지시오.

pt.L: E, quando você acabar de ler este rolo, amarre nele uma pedra e jogue-o no meio do Eufrates,
pt.B: Quando você terminar de ler este rolo, amarre nele uma pedra e jogue-o no meio do Eufrates,
pt.R: Quando você terminar de ler este rolo, amarre uma pedra nele. Jogue-o no meio do rio Eufrates.

decisions.choice: tie a stone to it and throw it: an acted sign of Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: Like the loincloth of 13:1-11 and the broken jar of 19:1-13, the act shows what the words say: as the scroll sinks, so will Babylon (verse 64). Revelation 18:21 takes up the sign: an angel throws a great millstone into the sea and says Babylon will be thrown down like it.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates: the river of Babylon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the river, Perath, the Euphrates, which ran through the city of Babylon (13:4; 46:2).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the river's name here, not "the River", so every level says "the Euphrates"; Readable adds "River".

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כָּ֠כָה תִּשְׁקַ֨ע בָּבֶ֤ל וְלֹֽא־תָקוּם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ וְיָעֵ֑פוּ עַד־הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and you will say: Thus will sink Babylon and not rise because of the disaster that I [am] bringing on her, and they will grow weary. Until here [are the] words of Jeremiah.

en.L: and say, 'Thus Babylon will sink and not rise, because of the disaster that I am bringing on her, and they will grow weary.'" Thus far [are] the words of Jeremiah.
en.B: and say, 'So Babylon will sink and rise no more, because of the disaster I am bringing on her, and they will grow weary.'" Here the words of Jeremiah end.
en.R: Then say, 'In the same way Babylon will sink and never come up again, because of the disaster I am bringing on her. And they will grow weary.'" This is the end of Jeremiah's words.

es.L: y di: “Así se hundirá Babilonia y no se levantará, a causa del mal que yo traigo sobre ella, y se cansarán”». Hasta aquí [son] las palabras de Jeremías.
es.B: y di: “Así se hundirá Babilonia y no volverá a levantarse, a causa de la calamidad que traigo sobre ella, y se cansarán”». Aquí terminan las palabras de Jeremías.
es.R: Luego di: “De la misma manera se hundirá Babilonia y nunca volverá a salir, por la desgracia que traigo sobre ella. Y se cansarán”». Aquí terminan las palabras de Jeremías.

fr.L: et dis : “Ainsi s’enfoncera Babylone, et elle ne se relèvera pas, à cause du malheur que je fais venir sur elle, et ils s’épuiseront.” » Jusqu’ici [sont] les paroles de Jérémie.
fr.B: et dis : “C’est ainsi que Babylone s’enfoncera et ne se relèvera plus, à cause du malheur que je fais venir sur elle, et ils s’épuiseront.” » Ici finissent les paroles de Jérémie.
fr.R: Puis dis : “Babylone s’enfoncera de la même manière et ne remontera jamais, à cause du malheur que je fais venir sur elle. Et ils s’épuiseront.” » Ici s’arrêtent les paroles de Jérémie.

ko.B: 그리고 이렇게 말하시오. '내가 바빌론에 내리는 재앙 때문에, 바빌론이 이렇게 가라앉아 다시는 떠오르지 못할 것이다. 그들은 지쳐 쓰러질 것이다.'" 예레미야의 말은 여기서 끝난다.

pt.B: e diga: 'Assim a Babilônia vai afundar e não vai mais se levantar, por causa da desgraça que estou trazendo sobre ela, e eles se cansarão.'" Aqui terminam as palavras de Jeremias.
pt.R: Depois diga: 'Do mesmo jeito a Babilônia vai afundar e nunca mais vai subir, por causa da desgraça que estou trazendo sobre ela. E eles vão se cansar.'" Aqui terminam as palavras de Jeremias.

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary: probably a phrase repeated by mistake from verse 58
alternatives: part of what Seraiah is to say
decisions.reason: The words end verse 58, where they make sense: the nations wear themselves out for nothing. Here they do not fit the sentence. They may have been copied as a marker of where the poem ended, before the story of verses 59-64 was placed after it, and then left in the text. The Greek translation lacks them (this is from general knowledge). They are kept here because they are in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: I am bringing: the LORD's own words, spoken by Seraiah
decisions.reason: Seraiah's words turn into the LORD's own word, as the prophet's message does elsewhere: the "I" is the LORD.

decisions.choice: thus far the words of Jeremiah: the end of the book's collection of his words
decisions.reason: The note marks the end of Jeremiah's words. Chapter 52 is an appendix from the history of the kings, nearly the same as 2 Kings 24:18-25:30, telling of Jerusalem's fall and of King Jehoiachin's release in Babylon. It shows that Jeremiah's word came true. The Greek translation lacks this note (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary kept inside Seraiah's words; the quotation closes
decisions.reason: The phrase stands where the Hebrew has it (m1), at the end of the quoted words. Readable sets it as a sentence of its own. Jeremiah's speech, opened in verse 61, closes here, before the closing note.

decisions.choice: y se cansarán, inside Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: The phrase from the end of verse 58 is kept inside the quoted words, before the note that Jeremiah's words end here (chapter 52 is an appendix).

decisions.choice: Ta (the LORD's words inside Seraiah's)
decisions.reason: The disaster "I am bringing" is the LORD's: Seraiah repeats God's own word, so Vietnamese says "Ta".

decisions.choice: "내가 ... 내릴" in 해라체 inside Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: these are the LORD's own words spoken by Seraiah, so they keep God's first person and 해라체.
